summary: Close 10-23: equity $600.92 (day -$3.82, +0.15% since start vs SPY -0.85%), with all 13 positions roughly flat to slightly down in a tech sell-off, so there was no news-driven shock in the book. The one company-specific catalyst we flagged for today's buys resolved cleanly: VRSN reported 10-22 (8-K 2.02 and 10-Q filed; EPS $2.35 missed $2.41, sales $443M beat, FY26 sales guide raised to $1.755B-$1.760B), Citigroup raised its PT to $345 from $325 this morning, and the position closed +3.7% on its fill. SAM also resolved (8-K 2.02 on 10-22: adj EPS beat, sales missed slightly, shipments/depletions guidance cut while adj EPS guidance was raised), which closes out the high-risk flag carried since 10-20. No 4.01, 4.02 or large 1.01/2.01 items appear for any holding or candidate, and no BTC/ETH exchange failure or new adverse regulatory action turned up (the Circle-investor suit against Trump and World Liberty Financial is political and not a regulatory action on BTC). Macro headlines that matter are the Iran/Houthi escalation (BTC fell to about $81-82k), Brent near $111-114, 10-year yield dropping below 5% with long bonds rallying despite a hot PPI, and the Fed meeting next week.

Today's two largest daily losers by percentage (CARG -3.7%, FAST -1.7%) have no company-specific news in the 72-hour window, so their moves look market or sector driven, not news driven.
